page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-75s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, the system includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 75 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The processor architecture supports hardware-level features such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA, with a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark results demonstrate a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves a strong single-core CPU performance score of 2929.97 in stress-ng tests, placing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance is weaker, scoring 5812.19 in stress-ng, which falls into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also constrained, with a weak PassMark memory score of 1687.01 and read-only memory bandwidth measuring 267.12 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 38.07 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Large block write memory bandwidth is average at 34.24 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, registering 27.69 GB/sec and 11.33 GB/sec respectively.

The instance exhibits poor performance in database operations and static web serving, with PassMark database operations scoring 935.72 and static web serving throughput reaching 2.39 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 10%. Redis SET operations are also weak at 3.82 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning, the instance processes 135M model prompts at a weak 203.02 tokens per second, though text generation for the same model is average at 87.92 tokens per second. Given these performance characteristics, the instance is suited for single-threaded compute tasks, lightweight utility services, and development environments rather than high-throughput database hosting or intensive web serving.
